title: Despotate of Arta
capsule: The Despotate of Arta was the political successor state in Epirus to the earlier Despotate of Epirus, reconstituted under the Tocco dynasty of Italian origin after the destruction wrought by the Albanian migrations and Serbian expansion in the mid-fourteenth century. Governed from the fortress city of Arta on the Arachthos River, the despotate under Carlo I Tocco (r. 1411–1429) reunited most of Epirus and briefly seized Ioannina in 1411, reaching the apogee of Tocco power. Carlo I also held Cephalonia and Zakynthos as Count Palatine, making the Tocco dominion the principal Latin power in western Greece. The Ottoman advance under Murad II extinguished the despotate's independence in 1449, with Arta itself falling by 1449 and the surrounding territory fully absorbed shortly after.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is moderately attested through Byzantine chronicles and Venetian diplomatic correspondence, but the despotate's fluctuating inland boundaries with Albanian clans and the Ottoman frontier are imprecisely mapped.
